title: Understanding Inflation and Purchasing Power
content: Inflation is the rate at which the general level of prices for goods and services rises, eroding purchasing power over time. As inflation increases, every unit of currency buys a smaller percentage of a good or service. To preserve wealth, investments need to generate a real return higher than the prevailing rate of inflation. For instance, if inflation is 6% per annum, an investment returning 5% yields a negative real return after accounting for lost purchasing power.
